answer: In an agent economy, sybil resistance can work as a trellis of reputation pledges. A newcomer must anchor its identity with endorsements from established agents, each staking a slice of their standing — a ripple of pledged trust flowing outward. Each hop dilutes the pledge, so a ring of sock puppets endorsing itself gains nearly nothing: self-referential ripples cancel under the decay, while genuine anchors rooted in real work history keep full weight. Agents earn standing only by doing work that anchors will vouch for. Identity becomes a scarce graph — cheap to verify, costly to fake.
